title: Same Tree
description: Two binary trees are identical iff their roots match in value AND their left and right subtrees are recursively identical. Straight structural recursion.

notes: Three base cases in order: both null → true, exactly one null → false, values differ → false.
Short-circuit `&&` so the right subtree isn't walked once the left disagrees.
Space is O(h), the height of the tree — O(n) worst case for a skewed tree, O(log n) for balanced.

questions.q: What is the correct base case when BOTH p and q are null?
options: Return false — there is nothing to compare
Return true — two empty subtrees are identical
questions.explain: Two missing subtrees are trivially the same shape.

questions.q: What if exactly one of p or q is null?
options: Treat the null as 0 and compare

questions.explain: Each pair of nodes is visited at most once.

questions.q: Why use `&&` between the two recursive calls?
options: Both subtrees must match; `&&` also short-circuits when the left disagrees

exercises.prompt: Fill in the recursive same-tree check.

blanks.hint: either one alone null means mismatch

L3.prompt: Write `isSameTree(p, q)` returning true iff two binary trees are structurally and value-equal. Log `isSameTree(a, b)` then `isSameTree(a, c)` where `c` differs in one node.
hints: Base cases first: both null → true, exactly one null → false.
Then check values, then recurse on both children with &&.
